title: Parsing an entry immediately followed by a termination marker
statement: Fix a width $w \ge 1$ and an index $\mathrm{idx} < w$, together with a direction bit $\mathrm{dir}$ and an arbitrary list of remaining entries $\mathrm{rest}$. Parsing the list that begins with the entry $(\mathrm{idx}, \mathrm{dir})$, followed immediately by the termination marker $(w, \mathrm{false})$, and then by $\mathrm{rest}$, produces the triple $(\mathrm{idx}, \mathrm{dir}, \mathrm{true})$ — with $\mathrm{idx}$ viewed as an element of $\{0, \dots, w-1\}$ and the final component recording that this entry is marked — prepended to the parse of $\mathrm{rest}$.
hypotheses_covered: the list has the shape (idx, dir) :: (w, false) :: rest, i.e. the entry is immediately followed by the marker (w, false)
replaced:
Equational lemma: if an entry $(idx, dir)$ with $idx < w$ is immediately
followed by the marker $(w, \mathrm{false})$, then $\mathrm{parseAux}$ emits the
triple $(\langle idx, h\rangle, dir, \mathrm{true})$ followed by the parse of the
rest.
